Core FY25–FY26 P&L, balance stocks and cash flows reconcile. EPS denominators and one ageing caption conflict but are explicitly bounded; actual issued shares replace EPS denominators. Restrained forward stress halts discretionary plant spending, retains maintenance/tax/interest/debt and uses no new supplemental facility; it survives with existing CC renewal from modeled base/bear cutoff anchors. Nonrenewal and deep stacked shocks can fail. Deep 25% AR/20% inventory loss plus 30% sales/5% margin is a boundary, not supported routine stress: it exceeds disclosed over-six-month AR exposure and lacks inventory-loss history. A separate 20% decline from reported FY26 to ₹93.66952 crore annual sales also survives with renewal from both anchors; operating-stock release is modeled, not guaranteed. No G3 cap is applied merely for that extreme or for haltable expansion. Verify real cutoff liquidity/drawing power before implementation.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Fascinate Textiles Limited, NSE SME FASCINATE, ISIN INE1Q2D01019. Information cutoff 20 October 2026; market endpoint 19 October. Standalone Indian Accounting Standards under the Companies(Accounting Standards) Rules(AS, not Ind AS); no subsidiary/associate or minority claim in the reviewed scope. Actual issued shares 13,760,893 and price ₹100.30 give market capitalization ₹138.0218 crore. Historical accounts end 31 March 2026: April–October is a modeled bridge, not a reported interim period. The shareholder horizon is exactly 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, nominal pretax, with no dividends and a 15% equity hurdle; 12%/18% alternatives are shown. The ₹5 lakh position is illustrative, not a recommended allocation. Identity/capital/official quote confidence is High; governance, comparable history, growth decomposition, capital returns and valuation inputs are Medium. Forecast uncertainty is High and separate from evidence confidence. G1/G2/G3/G4 are Conditional for the specific reasons in the gate register. No source search establishes universal legal clearance. [S1–S5][S7–S12]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Historical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 6, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6. Each has claim-linked facts and counterevidence in factor_audit. REV starts at 9 under the numerical growth schedule but is capped at 8 for Medium confidence and short comparable history. BQS=0.20×5+0.20×4+0.12×8+0.10×5+0.12×6+0.10×2+0.08×5+0.08×6=5.06. GQS raw=0.40×8+0.20×5+0.15×6+0.15×6+0.10×2=6.20; persistent CASH 2 caps final GQS at 5.00. IAS uses unrounded Q=5.06, R 10, D 3, P 5, L 5: 0.25×Q+0.35×10+0.20×3+0.10×5+0.10×5=6.3650. All composites have 100% factor coverage and no reweighting. R 10 is the explicit return-spread convention, not an arbitrary endorsement of accuracy; no extra narrative discount substitutes for correcting the model. All gates are conditional, with no evidenced severe governance failure or demonstrated unfinanceable ordinary stress. Display scores 5.1/5.0/6.4 use half-up rounding; ranking retains unrounded values. The model and quality judgments remain research heuristics, not validated return predictors. [S1–S6]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The issuer designs, manufactures and supplies garments, with children/infantwear together 60.38% of FY26 revenue and men’s/women’s garments adding 37.47%. Garments accounted for 97.86% of revenue versus 72.57% in FY25; residual fabrics/yarn contracted in mix. The company serves wholesalers/retailers and other business customers: B2B 99.75%, not primarily a consumer-brand retail franchise. Its Barasat, West Bengal unit coordinates cutting, selected stitching/printing/finishing and quality control, while general stitching and knitting/dyeing or other processes can be outsourced. Revenue is recognized on sale of goods under its AS policies; cash arrives later through receivables. Economics depend on order realization, raw-material/yarn cost, conversion work, rejection rates, labor utilization and financing of stock/credit. Inventory at ₹48.13 crore and receivables ₹35.28 crore are central operating assets, not incidental balance-sheet lines. FY26 sales were 96.74% domestic and 3.26% export; West Bengal supplied 67.01% and Karnataka 21.25% of total revenue. Domestic concentration matters more today than the aspirational export story. [S1]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The credible advantage is coordination and reliable delivery of designs/finishing to established customers. Mechanism: repeat buyer relationships and specialized in-house processes can reduce procurement friction. Evidence: disclosed relationships from 2019/2022/2023 and production scaling. Durability: unmeasured because contract duration, retention cohorts, rejection rates, switching penalties and price premiums are not disclosed. Failure mode: a larger buyer changes vendor or squeezes margin while inventory and outsourced commitments remain. Top 5/top 10 customers were 56.32%/72.99% in FY26, improved from 68.75%/93.22% in FY25, but still concentrated. Top 5/top 10 suppliers were 42.73%/55.86%, so supply cost/timing can also matter. There is no verified market-share denominator or unique-technology barrier; entrant replication costs/timing are ND, not assumed trivial. Iris Clothings is a useful kidswear comparator but owns the DOREME brand and distributor/retail proposition. Kewal Kiran combines manufacturing with established brands and retail reach. Their economics do not justify importing a branded-apparel multiple into a 99.75% B2B supplier. No current peer valuation table is fabricated from mismatched dates or FY25 market prices. MOAT 4 reflects these company-specific limits, not a blanket garment-sector penalty. [S1][S14][S15]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue was ₹21.8535/28.8802/60.2473/117.0869 crore in FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26. The reported three-year CAGR is 74.98%, but two related partnerships were taken over effective January 2024, so it is not a constant-perimeter organic CAGR. FY24 contains only three months of their activity, versus full FY25. The appropriate recent comparison is FY25–FY26: 94.34% growth and ₹56.8396 crore added. FY25 added ₹31.3671 crore but its 108.61% growth is perimeter-affected. Five-/ten-year CAGRs, TTM YoY and a comparable latest interim financial growth rate are ND. Garment production rose from 1.906 m to 3.108 m to 5.762 m pieces; FY26 growth 85.39% supports a volume component, but production is not invoiced units. Garment mix shifted from 72.57% to 97.86%; price, mix, inventory build and sales-volume effects cannot be cleanly isolated. Reported utilization 106.70% is based on double-shift 5.4 m capacity and includes outsourced production, so it is not proof of impossible output. The proposed plant targets a doubling of aggregate capacity, not a verified current doubling. Management’s August release reports ₹1.9072 crore exports through August 2026, including ₹1.0902 crore deemed exports, and approximately ₹12 crore September–December order book. Neither is total-company interim sales, a cash receipt or an independently checked contract backlog. [S1][S2][S10]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Growth currently consumes capital faster than it produces cash. FY25–FY26 invested capital grew from ₹29.0664 to ₹61.0628 crore, mainly working capital; a further ₹12.5034 crore plant project is proposed. The accounting incremental post-tax return proxy is 30.66%, not a project IRR, and must be tested against realized collections. The model uses an analytical 13–18% nominal INR capital-cost range, reflecting concentrated-customer equity risk and disclosed bank/NBFC borrowing costs; it is not an observed issuer WACC and differs from the 15% shareholder hurdle. Base growth slows to 30/24/18/15/12% in FY27–FY31, followed by 10% in FY32. EBITDA margins 18/18/17.5/17.5/17.5/17.5% normalize below FY26. Those remain assumptions: scaling terminal revenue to ₹302.26 crore requires capacity completion, further outsourcing and/or price/mix gains. With unchanged garment mix/realization, a simple production proxy would exceed the announced doubled 10.8 m capacity; roughly 5% annual realization/mix gains lessen, but do not eliminate, that gap. This is not independent unit-economics proof. Maintenance capex 0.8% of sales is an estimate, not disclosed maintenance spending or automatically D&A; 0.9–1% and project overruns/delays appear in other cases. New plant land/permits were pending at RHP and July 2027 is the management target. Capacity plans and IPO cash improve the possible runway; recurring cash conversion and customer breadth must validate it. Persistent CASH 2 caps GQS at 5 despite high measured sales growth. [S1][S3][S10]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters and promoter group held 68.4% in the 21 August post-issue pattern; public holding was 31.6% across 1,948 public shareholders. The listing archive separately showed 68.8% locked and 31.20% free: these are distinct legal/ownership measures. No pledge, NDU, other encumbrance, convertible, warrant or outstanding ESOP was declared in that dated pattern; it is not a claim about unknown subsequent changes. FY26 director remuneration ₹0.2405 crore was about 1.59% of PAT; family employment and promoter-linked transactions are disclosed. RPT sales including GST were ₹3.6358 crore with Arihant Fashion and ₹20.3497 crore with Karnika; receipts and closing balances are disclosed. These gross tax-inclusive figures cannot be treated as a precise fraction of net reported revenue, and their existence is not evidence of abuse. The January 2024 partnership acquisitions used 1.248867 crore of noncash share consideration; conflict-of-interest and price/value assessment remains relevant despite disclosure.

Governance execution is mixed. Disclosed delays include a 647-day ADT-1 filing,7-day AOC-4 and 31/12-day PAS-3 delays, alongside tax/social-contribution delays. Issuer explanations and subsequent filing/payment statements are recorded, not independently certified. Auditor transitions were described as earlier auditor preoccupation and the need for a peer-reviewed auditor; the restatement report does not describe audit qualifications requiring adjustment. The 13 October appointment is secretarial/internal assurance and RTA, not a statutory-auditor resignation. CARE’s fresh register as of 18 October lists an unaccepted CARE BB+; Stable rating on ₹22.4 crore bank facilities, non-acceptance dated 19 December 2025. This is a historical unaccepted rating, not a current accepted opinion, default, noncooperation or misconduct finding. No rationale or reason for non-acceptance was retrieved. RHP says no credit rating obtained; the distinction between accepted rating and unaccepted register entry is not silently converted into a contradiction or concealment accusation. The small pending TDS disclosure and EPCG contingent guarantee are separately modeled. No serious allegation from unsourced commentary is adopted. [S1][S3][S4][S11–S13]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The historical financial table and exact definitions follow this manuscript; the linked model retains all opening claims. FY26 reported PAT ₹15.0970 crore becomes PBT ₹21.3445 crore; adding D&A ₹0.5864 and finance ₹2.2957, less interest received ₹0.0248, gives cash-flow profit before working capital ₹24.2018 crore. Payables add ₹17.1269 and other current liabilities ₹0.3937; receivables absorb ₹17.9470 and inventory ₹32.6633; loans/advances release ₹0.0988. Cash generated before taxes is−₹8.7891 crore, and ₹2.0846 tax paid gives CFO−₹10.8737. Cash capex ₹0.4949 is investing cash, not the explanation for negative CFO. The reported FCF proxy is−₹11.3686 crore before financing-classified interest; subtracting ₹2.2957 finance cash gives−₹13.6643 crore. FY25–FY26 cumulative CFO/PAT is−69.11%; FY24–FY26 is-84.51%. Older FY23 also had−₹0.3192 crore CFO, but its pre-acquisition perimeter precludes a clean four-year organic ratio.

Inventory increased more than threefold to ₹48.1293 crore, including ₹15.7566 raw materials, ₹23.9549 work in process and ₹8.4178 finished goods. No inventory ageing/realization test was located. Receivables ₹35.2774 crore include ₹4.5397 crore over six months from due date versus ₹0.0763 crore in FY25; no doubtful provision is disclosed. The schedule header is 31 March 2026 but one total-row caption says 31 December 2025: total matches the FY26 balance, yet date-caption clarification is warranted. Balances are subject to confirmation/reconciliation under note 55, with management asserting realizability. This supports collection stress, not a finding that all balances are bad. Ending AR/revenue days is about 110.0 and ending inventory/revenue days 150.0; they are revenue-denominator proxies, not a fabricated cash-conversion cycle. Compatible complete COGS/credit-purchase and ageing information is insufficient for a precise comparable CCC here.

Operating capital is ONWC plus operating fixed assets/CWIP/land/deposits, excluding cash, government balances, related advances and income-tax financing. FY25/FY26 IC ₹29.0664/₹61.0628; 29% normalized-tax NOPAT ₹6.8746/₹16.6844; FY26 average-IC ROIC 37.02%, pre-tax ROCE 52.15%. Incremental proxy 30.66% usesΔNOPAT ₹9.8098/ΔIC ₹31.9964. The investment cross-check is capex−D&A+ΔONWC, with the small deposit/rounding residual separately retained. Government-asset inclusion lowers the proxy to about 29.8%; it does not cure negative cash realization. One comparable interval and old-asset margin gains are not project IRR. Comparable 3/5-year incremental and commissioned-new-plant returns are ND.

The model’s EBITDA convention adds all finance cost back: FY26₹24.0855 versus issuer KPI ₹24.0039. The ₹0.0816 difference equals loan-processing/bank charges; FY25 difference ₹0.2168 similarly matches those charges. Forecast financing fees are then charged explicitly once. FY24 KPI gap is less clean and not used for the current margin base. EPS note denominators also conflict: FY26₹14.66 versus ₹11.04 elsewhere. Use verified issued 13,760,893 shares, yielding historical PAT/current-share ₹10.9702, not a fictional reconciled reported EPS. The 6: 1 bonus is not economic dilution; cash rights and the actual fresh IPO increase outside capital. FY24 noncash takeover share/premium amounts appear in financing cash-flow presentation; published totals reconcile, but acquisition-specific cash classification remains unresolved and FY24 is not treated as organic proof. [S1–S4]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Observed price ₹100.30×13,760,893 actual shares gives ₹138.0218 crore equity value. Historical FY26 PAT/current shares implies 9.14×P/E; this is a backward diagnostic on current diluted capital, not a forecast or an assertion that March cash is current. No mechanically combined current EV/EBITDA is presented using pre-IPO debt and ignoring IPO cash. The monthly linked model starts 31 March 2026 and explicitly reconstructs to entry 19 October before forecasting five shareholder years. Gross fresh IPO cash ₹52.20976 is assumed received 24 August; ₹12.6236 OFS belongs to sellers and is excluded. Assumed company fees ₹5 crore, varied to ₹3/₹7, leave ₹47.20976 net: WC ₹25.1524, capex ₹12.3541, debt ₹2.6777 and residual ₹7.02556. Actual net proceeds/fee allocation/utilization are still ND. WC proceeds pay eligible positive operating cash costs, never directly the related-party debt; plant and debt pots retain their separate uses. Land advance ₹0.05 is already paid; remaining plant cash ₹12.4534 includes the ₹0.0993 internally funded GST gap, without invented credit recovery.

Opening tax ₹6.2501 is paid once on assumed 30 September, not lost by excluding it from WC. Government balances ₹1.8762 are not presumed offsettable tax credits; base excludes recovery and bull recovers them on a stated 2028 date. Lien FD ₹0.3599 is neither spending cash nor terminal surplus. Opening expense/statutory/customer balances remain WC exactly once; all principal and interest are dated. Related/company loans use explicit assumed rates and maturities because full terms are unavailable. Current bank/NBFC principal and later maturities are paid; IPO debt money repays remaining eligible NBFC/bank amounts, not original balances already amortized. CC limit ₹20.8 in one table conflicts with ₹15.8 elsewhere; 9.75% base rate and a lower-limit/no-renewal alternative avoid silent optimism. All scenarios charge interest on new debt and 1% supplemental draw fees. Supplemental limits ₹12/₹18/₹45 crore are hypothetical, not sanctioned financing; the base and bull do not draw them, the bear does, and the severe rescue case is explicitly an algebraic counterfactual. No future equity rescue or undated debt plug is assumed.

Funded bear/base/bull five-year nominal pretax IRRs are-1.71%/27.39%/49.12%; severe equity is zero. Terminal values use 365-day EBITDA to 19 October 2031, not unearned full FY32 profit. EV plus accumulated unrestricted cash above ₹0.5 crore less debt, accrued current tax, ₹0.0473 DTL and conservative ₹0.0082 EPCG contingent reserve yields shareholder value; normal WC/PPE are already in EV and never added again. Bear/base/bull exits 5×/7×/9× are analyst assumptions spanning a commodity/manufacturing valuation range, not observed comparable medians. No dividends, personal tax or dealing costs are presumed; 2%/5% exit-cost haircuts are shown separately.

The 15% hurdle requires ₹201.7391 per share after five years. Holding the base cash/debt/tax path fixed, required exit EBITDA multiple is 3.495×. The fully rerun growth-hurdle crossing lowers each annual growth assumption by roughly 14.54 pp, but cash then rises partly because less working capital is needed. That is not proof that no growth is required or that trapped inventory is freely distributable.12%/18% hurdles, exit multiples 3/5/9/11×, margin−3 pp, receivables+30 days, inventory+45 days, persistent opening WC ratios, cashbuffer ₹3 crore, project+25%, fee/tax timing, government recovery and two-way margin/receivables grids are retained. A 3× exit pushes unchanged-base return below 15%; the funded bear already misses. Large terminal cash and operating normalization are doing substantial valuation work. [S1][S3][S5][S6]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that garments cease selling. It is that buyers delay or reject orders while material/WIP already exists, old receivables fail to collect, suppliers shorten terms and margin normalization coincides with expansion spending. The FY26 cash bridge demonstrates exposure to this mechanism; top 10 concentration and the over-six-month receivable increase provide issuer-specific support. Debt and fresh equity can fund growth without fixing its economics. If cash cannot service lenders/taxes, owners bear dilution, distressed asset realization and potentially zero residual value; low reported P/E is not downside protection. The funded bear includes 10% opening AR and 5% inventory losses plus project delay/overrun, and needs about ₹3.04 crore supplemental debt. Its IRR is conditional on that unavailable-to-verify facility. Without funding, the model stops and assigns no fabricated terminal value or IRR.

Pre-entry failures in alternative April–October bridges only falsify those unverified reconstructions; they do not establish an issuer default. Forward tests are separate. A restrained survival test starts at the modeled cutoff, halts all discretionary future plant spending, leaves its unused earmark ring-fenced, maintains essential capex 0.8% of sales, pays tax/interest/principal, freezes sales after a 20% shock to the modeled FY27 run rate and uses 10% EBITDA margin with 10% AR/5% inventory losses. It survives with existing CC renewal and no new supplemental debt after entry, from both base and bear modeled anchors; the bear anchor itself had hypothetical pre-entry funding later repaid. A separate test anchors the 20% decline to reported FY26 sales instead, holding annual sales at ₹93.66952 crore: it also survives with renewal from both cutoff anchors, and from the base anchor without renewal. This lower-sales survival relies partly on gradual release of collectible working capital after the stated losses, not guaranteed liquidation at book value. Without CC renewal, some tests breach the chosen ₹0.5 crore buffer before actual cash goes negative; those are explicitly liquidity-buffer warnings, not automatically missed obligations. Deep 30% sales/5% margin/25% AR/20% inventory stacking can produce negative essential cash even with renewal, but exceeds the measured over-six-month AR share and has no verified inventory-loss history. It is a severe boundary, not the demonstrated credible-stress failure required for a G3 cap. Hence G3 remains Conditional, not Clear and not an asserted actual insolvency. No project-cancellation penalty is assumed because contracts are unavailable; inability to halt committed spending would weaken that survival result. Actual post-IPO cash, drawing power and collection evidence could change the gate immediately. [S1][S3][S12]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold per-share outcomes over five years require 41.47% and 58.49% annualized price growth. The base modeled terminal price is only about 3.35× entry; the bull about 7.37×, contingent on 50/35/28/22/18% FY27–FY31 sales growth, sustained 20–21% EBITDA, better working-capital ratios and 9× terminal EBITDA. That bull is a demanding upside scenario, not a supported probability. Lower the bull exit multiple to 5× and its outcome falls sharply; the exact bridge below prevents relabeling operating growth as stock-price growth. Holding the base cash/claims fixed,5×/10× require much greater EBITDA and revenue, but that shortcut ignores the extra WC and capacity required and is labeled algebra only. Announced doubled capacity and the existing outsourcing model do not independently demonstrate the much larger production, customer diversification and finance needed. A fresh equity raise could enable expansion while reducing the current holder’s per-share outcome; none is assumed in the displayed paths.5× is possible but demanding; 10× is speculative/unsupported at this five-year horizon on the reviewed evidence. There is no numerical success probability and no market-share claim without a dated denominator. [S1][S3][S5][S10]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before an implementation conclusion, obtain the first post-IPO balance sheet/cash-flow statement, final issuer-borne offer costs, bank-wise eligible IPO deployment and unused earmark balances. Reconcile ₹20.8/₹15.8 crore sanction descriptions with current drawing power, collateral, renewal dates and amortization schedules. Obtain customer ageing and subsequent receipts, inventory ageing/WIP completion, supplier-credit changes and RPT collection terms. In the next reported period, require absolute CFO and working-capital movement evidence rather than PAT alone; two consecutive comparable periods of cash-positive operations and declining overdue balances would justify reassessing CASH, not an isolated turnover announcement.

By the July 2027 management plant target, check land title, permits, contractor orders, spend versus budget, trial/commercial production and independently reconcilable capacity. A delay is not automatically failure before the target, but a material cost overrun or inability to redirect legally restricted funds changes the funding model. Check whether September–December export orders turn into sales and cash, excluding deemed exports from claims about new overseas customers. At each results/shareholding cycle, update actual shares, pledges/encumbrances, RPT balances, auditor observations, open tax matters and any accepted credit rating. Before any order, recheck current lot, trade-to-trade/ASM status, price band, order-book spread/depth and the intended position size. Kill/re-underwrite triggers: an observed unfinanceable essential cash shortfall, material unsupported receivable write-off, unexplained related-party cash outflow, adverse audit access/reliability finding, or economic dilution that invalidates per-share returns. Ordinary price volatility alone is not thesis evidence. [S1][S3][S4][S8][S10–S12][S16]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Under the exact v3 matrix, BQS 5.06 and IAS 6.365 mean speculative or mixed-quality watchlist. GQS is 5.0 after the cash cap; this fails the compounder designation by a wide margin. The high conditional R is not a buy recommendation: current audited liquidity is old, financing/collections are conditional, and 17 single-price sessions undermine an apparently easy turnover exit. The useful next action is verification of post-IPO cash conversion, actual plant funding and bank availability, not adopting the bull endpoint as a target. A lower price improves return arithmetic but cannot cure bad assets or a funding failure; stronger collections and completed capacity can improve the business case even without rerating. No position-size, suitability, tax or portfolio conclusion is made without the user’s circumstances. A material G2 issue would make IAS NS; an evidenced credible G3 failure would cap IAS at 3; effective untradeability would make a new-purchase IAS NS. Those overrides must be applied if supported, not presumed from SME status or avoided with hypothetical rescue finance. [S1][S3][S5][S8]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence consists of the latest RHP and earlier DRHP, NSE listing/shareholding archive, dated issuer exchange releases, official daily bhavcopies/security/surveillance files and CARE’s unaccepted-rating register. Iris and Kewal Kiran annual reports are used only for qualitative business-model comparison. No third-party price target, unverified allegation or search snippet supplies a decisive score. RHP financial statement numbers are distinguished from issuer KPIs and management projections; exact scripts and source hashes accompany the private dossier. Core source/input confidence is Medium; recoverability, current cash, contracts and future capacity carry high forecast uncertainty. Unavailable final IPO expenses/utilization, claim sub-ledgers, precise loan schedules, plant approval/commitment status, receivable collection proof, inventory ageing, customer retention and live execution depth are specific gaps, not invented neutral scores. Cash/debt/tax/contingent claims each have one treatment. The small EPCG reserve is an analytical completeness correction, not a new issuer accounting finding. Research is complete within these disclosed limits, but no public publication or Git write has occurred. Sensitive factual wording is separately registered for parent review before consequential publication. [S1–S16]

GOV.reason: Mixed disclosed governance: adequate restated assurance and IPO disclosure, but compliance execution and related-party oversight need follow-through. No substantiated diversion or abusive minority transaction found in reviewed primary records.
material_facts: FY26 related-party sales are ₹23.9855 crore including GST; counterparties and receipts are disclosed.
ROC filings include a 647-day ADT-1 delay and shorter AOC-4/PAS-3 delays; tax/social-contribution delays are also disclosed.
GOV.contrary_evidence: Audit report describes no qualifications requiring restatement; director remuneration ₹0.2405 crore is only about 1.59% of FY26 PAT. Auditor change reasons are disclosed, not evidence of conflict.

MOAT.reason: A manufacturing/service capability with customer relationships, not demonstrated brand pricing power, proprietary technology or hard switching costs. Scale and quality coordination help, but replication and buyer bargaining remain credible.
material_facts: B2B supplied 99.75% of FY26 revenue; top 10 customers 72.99%.
General stitching, knitting/dyeing and parts of processing are outsourced; no verified premium, market-share denominator or switching-cost quantification.
MOAT.contrary_evidence: Several disclosed customers have relationships dating to 2019/2022/2023; in-house specialized finishing and quality control offer execution value. Concentration fell versus FY25.

REV.reason: FY25–FY26 same-perimeter revenue growth 94.34% maps to raw 9. Final 8 applies the mandatory Medium/short-relevant-history ceiling, not a small-size penalty. FY23–FY26 CAGR is shown only as a perimeter-distorted diagnostic.
material_facts: Comparable annual revenue addition ₹56.8396 crore; revenue reached ₹117.0869 crore.
Garment production rose 85.39% in FY26; garments expanded to 97.86% of revenue from 72.57%.
REV.contrary_evidence: Production is not sales volume and price/mix/currency decomposition is not separately audited; FY24 includes only a partial year of two acquired partnerships. No comparable interim financial result is available.

DUR.reason: Plausible garment demand and a funded capacity plan support a runway, but neither customer breadth nor independently validated future capacity establish durable high growth.
material_facts: Planned new plant is intended to double aggregate capacity, with ₹12.3541 crore IPO allocation.
Existing garment utilization 106.7% includes outsourcing; FY26 domestic sales 96.74% and West Bengal 67.01% limit diversification.
DUR.contrary_evidence: Export activity and management’s approximately ₹12 crore September–December order book could broaden demand; they do not prove recognized revenue, collections or repeat orders.

CAP.reason: Strong accounting operating-return proxy but unproven incremental cash economics. FY25–FY26 observed incremental ROIC 30.66% exceeds an analytical INR nominal capital-cost range 13–18%; one interval cannot establish a plant/project IRR.
material_facts: NOPAT at 29% tax rose from ₹6.8746 to ₹16.6844 crore while operating invested capital rose from ₹29.0664 to ₹61.0628 crore.
FY26 average-IC ROIC 37.02% accompanies substantial inventory/receivable investment rather than cash harvesting.
CAP.contrary_evidence: Margin/utilization gains on old assets explain part of profit growth; plant is not yet commissioned, government-asset inclusion lowers returns, and full 3/5-year comparable windows are unavailable.

CASH.reason: Persistent inability to turn stated profits into operating cash is decisive. Applies GQS cap 5; not a capex-driven CFO explanation.
material_facts: FY25–FY26 cumulative CFO/PAT is−69.11%; all FY23–FY26 reported CFO observations are negative.
FY26 inventory absorbed ₹32.6633 crore and receivables ₹17.9470 crore, only partly offset by ₹17.1269 crore additional payables.
CASH.contrary_evidence: Revenue expansion legitimately needs working capital, and fresh IPO money can fund it. That finances the gap but does not demonstrate collections or recurring free cash flow.

BAL.reason: IPO materially improves potential funding, but large working stocks, uncertain post-issue cash and reliance on credit renewal prevent a resilience score above the middle band.
material_facts: March 2026 debt ₹26.021 crore versus unrestricted cash ₹0.4559 crore and taxprovision ₹6.2501 crore.
Gross fresh issue ₹52.20976 crore is real; OFS ₹12.6236 crore is never company cash. Restrained no-new-supplemental stress survives with existing CC renewal.
BAL.contrary_evidence: Unused CC availability/drawing power, actual net proceeds and utilization are not verified; severe combined collection/margin/refinancing shocks can breach essential cash funding. CARE record is historical unaccepted, not default evidence.

EXEC.reason: Two comparable years show real operating scaling; implementation credibility remains bounded because the principal funded expansion has not reached its promised date.
material_facts: Garment production increased from 3.108 million to 5.762 million pieces and reported sales nearly doubled.
Exports were disclosed in FY26 and increased through August 2026; the new plant timetable is July 2027.
EXEC.contrary_evidence: Land/approvals were pending at RHP; outsourcing complicates capacity attribution, working-capital conversion is poor, and no post-IPO utilization certificate or commissioning milestone was located.

EARN.reason: Profit growth is mainly operating, not incidental income, but margin normalization, receivable realizability and per-share presentation limit earnings durability.
material_facts: FY26 PAT ₹15.097 crore grew 159.8%; otherincome ₹0.1411 crore is small relative to PBT ₹21.3445 crore.
PAT margin rose from 9.65% to 12.89%; total-finance-cost EBITDA proxy rose from ₹10.1986 to ₹24.0855 crore.
EARN.contrary_evidence: Four negative CFO observations and ageing risk weaken economic validation. RHP EPS denominators conflict; current-share historical PAT/share is recomputed at ₹10.9702, not copied from ₹14.66 reported EPS.

R.reason: Conditional base IRR 27.3881% versus 15% hurdle gives +12.3881 pp, mechanically R 10. Growth slows sharply from FY26, margin normalizes below FY26, and all working capital/capex/tax/interest is funded. R 10 is not a probability or a validation of the assumptions.
material_facts: Actual post-IPO shares are used; base requires no hypothetical supplemental draw, but does assume facility availability and modeled deployment of fresh IPO funds.
R.contrary_evidence: Base returns depend on sustained collections, working-capital efficiency and plant/outsourcing execution. Bear return is negative; severe rescue counterfactual wipes equity. Unverified cutoff cash and absent interim accounts create high forecast uncertainty.

D.reason: Material capital-impairment and adverse-refinancing risk; the surviving restrained essential-operation case prevents treating every downturn as insolvency.
material_facts: Funded bear returns−1.7062% annually and requires peak supplemental debt about ₹3.04 crore.
Severe algebraically funded path loses all equity; no-new-supplemental severe path stops with a forward cash shortfall.
D.contrary_evidence: A restrained forward 20% sales shock,10% EBITDA margin,10% AR/5% inventory loss and halted growth capex survives without new supplemental debt if existing CC renews. This is meaningful counterevidence, not proven severe-stress immunity.

P.reason: The price permits a fair normalization case, but low apparent earnings multiples are not sufficient margin-of-safety evidence when cash conversion and terminal cash dominate.
material_facts: At ₹100.30, current-share FY26 P/E is 9.14×; basefixed-bridge 15% hurdle requires roughly 3.50× exit EBITDA.
A fully rerun lower-growth path meets 15% only with improving working-capital ratios and large accumulated cash; 3× exit on unchangedbase falls below 15%.
P.contrary_evidence: Initial shares/price are verified and several bounded sensitivities still clear 15%; however the bear misses the hurdle, and the reverse growth crossing is not proof that growth is unnecessary.

L.reason: Theoretical 0.97-day exit at 5% of conservative 39-session median starts L 9. Four explicit points are deducted for demonstrated one-price sessions/bands, low-PAN cautions, short history and lot/lock-in constraints.
material_facts: 17 of 39 official daily rows have identical high/low; one session traded only ₹4.50 lakh.
800 shares cost ₹80,240, or 16.05% of the ₹5 lakh reference; listing lock-in 68.8% and publicholding 31.6% are not interchangeable with freely tradeable float.
L.contrary_evidence: Every observed listed session had positive volume and median turnover ₹1.0322 crore; no suspension is inferred from masterstatus 6, which decodes as price discovery. Live depth/spread remains unavailable.

model_assumptions: FY27–FY32 revenue growth, EBITDA margins, WC stock/revenue ratios, capex, losses and exit multiples are analyst scenarios, not guidance or predictions. Other income, FD interest and dividends are zero in all forecast cases.

The IPO WC earmark funds positive gross operating cash payments after receipt, not merely net WC increases. This lets earmarked money pay its authorized use instead of incorrectly trapping it, but is not a claim that actual deployment was certified. It never directly repays related-party debt. The 0.0993 project GST gap is cash-funded internally, without an invented tax-credit recovery; reserves release proportionally, leaving overruns internally funded. Remaining project reserves fund only project spend and the debt reserve only NBFC/bank principal.

Borrowing interest is based on opening debt plus new draws for the full dated period; scheduled principal and sweeps are end-period. New supplemental draw fees are 1% and expensed. Spare unrestricted cash above 1 crore repays supplemental debt then cash credit; other debt follows dated repayments.

Tax is an assumed 29% of positive profit before impairment and additional legacy claims, after depreciation/interest/draw fees, paid at calendar-quarter ends. No impairment shield, loss carryforward, MAT credit or new DTA is assumed. Any closing accrued current tax and the opening DTL are exit deductions.

Opening inventory/AR impairments reduce recoverable opening stock first. The noncash P&L loss is added back once and replacement WC/foregone collections are cash-funded once. The impairment amount is not deducted a second time from terminal equity.

Existing PPE depreciation starts from 0.5864 crore/year and is capped at book value. New maintenance capex is depreciated over 10 years from the next period. Project building/machinery uses 30/15 years, land is not depreciated, and cost overruns scale depreciable assets. All depreciation is an economic scenario, not a tax-depreciation filing.

Terminal valuation on 19 October 2031 uses trailing-365-day EBITDA, never a full FY32 result not yet earned. EV plus unrestricted cash above the operating buffer less debt/current tax/DTL and the conservative 0.0082 EPCG contingent reserve yields equity, floored at zero. Normal WC/PPE are embedded in EV, not liquidated or added again. All 13,760,893 issued shares are used, no future equity raise is presumed.

All IRRs are five-year nominal pretax shareholder outcomes from the 19 October 2026 close, with no interim dividends, dealing costs or capital-gains tax. They apply only to funded conditional paths. They are not target prices, recommendations, assured financing or evidence of actual solvency. The severe rescue line is an algebraic counterfactual, not a creditworthy/debt-capacity conclusion; lender covenants and willingness are unknown.
valuation.not_forecast_guarantee: All forecast balances and cash/debt paths are conditional analyst scenarios, not reported post-IPO results or committed lender facilities. No IRR exists after an unfunded path stops.

limitations: There is no verified post-IPO cash balance or complete final offer-expense/utilisation statement at the 20 October 2026 cutoff. Gross fresh proceeds and issued shares are verified, but 24 August receipt and 5 crore fees (3/7 sensitivity) are scenario assumptions. OFS proceeds never enter company cash.

The opening balance sheet is 31 March 2026, not the valuation date. April–19 October 2026 is an unverified reconstruction, not reported interim performance. Any pre-cutoff financing failure only falsifies that assumed reconstruction, not the fact that the issuer listed or a finding of default.

Government balances of 1.8762 crore do not distinguish advance tax, TDS, GST or other claims. No automatic tax offset is taken. Opening income-tax liability 6.2501 is paid in full on an assumed date. Claim composition must be verified before replacing this conservative treatment.

Bank EMI schedules and complete NBFC prepayment terms were not available. Opening current bank principal 0.8041 and NBFC principal 0.9769 are explicitly paid monthly until prepaid; remaining bank short/long tranches clear by June 2027/June 2029. These are conservative analytical schedules, not certified lender amortisation tables.

Cash-credit sanction 20.8 crore in the RHP loan table conflicts with 15.8 crore in its objects narrative; 9% table pricing conflicts with a 9.75% note. Model uses the table limit with 9.75% base interest, a 15.8-limit sensitivity, and non-renewal alternative. Availability/drawing-power, collateral and annual renewal are not verified commitments. The 15.8-limit sensitivity removes new headroom above that amount without retroactively calling existing drawn debt; the separate February 2027 non-renewal case calls the facility.

Related-party and other-body-corporate loan rates/maturities are undisclosed. Model uses 9%/12% interest and dated March 2027/March 2028 repayment. NBFC prepayment charges are zero in baseline but a 2% charge sensitivity reduces eligible principal within the fixed earmark. Supplemental revolvers and their renewal are purely hypothetical, with 1% draw fees and 15%/17%/20% interest, not guaranteed financing.

Opening expense/statutory buckets have no complete sub-ledger separating employee, interest, capital-creditor and tax components. All disclosed balances remain in WC exactly once. No separate gratuity deficit is disclosed despite an actuarial policy; this is not proof of zero obligation. Additional 1 crore legacy-claim stress is explicit, not an issuer finding.

The pending TDS amount described in the RHP is approximately 0.08 lakh (14,130 less 5,721 paid = 8,409 rupees). Its inclusion within the 0.8933 crore statutory bucket is unverified. It is not blindly added twice; a separate 0.0008409 crore cash sensitivity tests the possibility it is outside the bucket. No post-RHP case status is asserted.

FY24 includes January 2024 partnership acquisitions for noncash shares (1.248867 crore consideration). The published cash-flow statement includes 1.2488 crore share/premium financing; the cash bridge mathematically reconciles but acquisition-specific cash-flow attribution is unresolved. FY24 is not an organic comparable growth base.

Land ownership, approvals and commissioning were pending at the RHP. Project cost/timing and revenue/margins are assumptions. Model contains no independently validated garment-capacity forecast or separate forecast of order-book conversion.

The 0.0082 crore unprovided customs/EPCG bank guarantee (RHP PDF 314 note 30) is conservatively reserved once at exit, not represented as a booked or currently payable liability. The amount is immaterial to conclusions; its inclusion corrects analytical claim coverage, not issuer accounting.

The restricted 0.3599 crore lien FD is never spendable or terminal surplus. Security deposits/related advances and unverified government recovery are excluded from exit additions. The related bank debt is nevertheless fully paid; release of the FD would be upside not assumed.

The forecast is a deterministic monthly/month-end economic model with dated issue, debt, tax and impairment events, not a daily treasury forecast. Revenue and operating balances are smoothly phased; seasonal and intra-period cash troughs could be worse. A 0.5 crore buffer is an assumption, with a 3 crore sensitivity.

The latest RHP covers FY24–FY26; the earlier DRHP additionally covers FY23 on a pre-acquisition perimeter. Only 39 listed observed sessions exist in the reviewed data. There is no invented five-year historical record, no zero-filled prelisting liquidity, and no executable bid/depth or future exit guarantee.
